In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BchX2 and BchNB subunits are structurally and functionally similar to the NifH and NifB subunits of nitrogenase, respectively, whereas the BchL subunit is not.
the electron transfer between subunit BchB and BchL is mediated by a hydrophobic interaction between the two subunits.
the BchX2 or ChlX2 subunits from the COR enzymes are functionally interchangeable with the L2 subunits of the DPOR enzymes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DPOR and COR enzymes are structurally related to nitrogenases and share a similar electron-transfer pathway, although the COR enzymes are more closely related to nitrogenases.

(BchNB)-BchL2 and (ChlNB)-ChlL2 of the DPOR system are homologous in terms of their interaction and that the BchX2 part of the COR system can substitute for the BchL or ChlL part of DPOR, but not vice versa.

(i) the interaction surface between BchL2 and BchNB is highly conserved between the two DPOR subunits, (ii) the electron-transferring subunit BchB is essential for the activity of DPOR, and (iii) the electron-transmitting subunit of COR is interchangeable with that of nitrogenase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electron-transferring subunit Bch/X2 of COR and DPOR is interchangeable, whereas the catalytic subunit (B/N)2 is not.

the interaction between the electron donor BchX or ChlL with the (BchNB or ChlNB)2 heterotetramer can be substituted for the interaction of the electron donor BChL2 or Chll2 with the (BChNB or ChlNb)2 heterotetermer.
